title: On obtaining the convex hull of quadratic inequalities via aggregations
contribution: Under a positive-definite-linear-combination (PDLC) condition, the convex hull of three quadratic inequalities is the intersection of (possibly infinitely many) aggregations with at most one negative eigenvalue, and counterexamples show the result does not extend to four quadratics or to the case without PDLC.
problem_entry: Aggregation is complete for linear systems (Farkas) and for two quadratics (Yildiran); the paper asks whether it still gives the hull for three or more quadratics (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Prove a new symmetric three-quadratic S-lemma by SDP duality plus Pataki/Barvinok rank reduction, then go from a separating hyperplane, through homogenization, to faux-separation of a semi-convex cone (Thm 2 p. 4; Lemma 1 p. 3; pp. 10-15).
assumptions: n >= 3, strict inequalities, PDLC, conv(S) != R^n; the closed case adds 'no low-dimensional components', which the authors call not easy to verify (pp. 4, 7-9).
proof_devices: SDP duality + rank reduction with a dimension case split (Barvinok if bounded, Pataki otherwise) for the symmetric S-lemma (pp. 10-11)
separating hyperplane -> homogenize -> restrict quadratics to the hyperplane -> S-lemma (Lemmas 2-3, pp. 12-13)
Yildiran's semi-convex cone / faux-separating hyperplane + Cauchy interlacing to get nu <= 1 (pp. 12, 14)
interior of an infinite intersection lemma + Modaresi-Vielma lemma for the closed case (pp. 15-16)

counterexamples: orthant-wise eigenvalue bound giving box [-8,8]^3, LP infeasibility certificate checked in exact arithmetic, polytope slicing, SDP-not-tight example, an infinite family of aggregations (pp. 17-24)
experiments: none as a section; numerical exploration only: plots, the true box estimated at [-1.23,1.23]^3, and a search that found no PDLC example needing infinitely many aggregations (pp. 6-9, 18)
positioning: Follows Yildiran's presentation and proof strategy and Modaresi-Vielma for the closed case; set apart from SDP-tightness results (Wang-Kilinc-Karzan) by an example where aggregations give the hull but the SDP is not tight (pp. 1-2, 7-8, 21-22).
writing: All results, examples, counterexamples and open questions come before the proofs; the demarcation is itself advertised as the contribution; specific hedges about the finiteness of Omega (pp. 2-9).
limits_future: Open: whether Omega is finite under PDLC, relaxing the no-low-dimensional-components condition, the role of PDLC; four or more constraints unlikely without more structure (p. 9).

title: Exploiting instance and variable similarity to improve learning-enhanced branching
contribution: For operational MILPs re-solved with slightly changing data (SCUC), training separate strong-branching-score regressors per variable or per variable group brings learned branching much closer to strong branching than a single model trained on the same data.
problem_entry: SCUC must be solved daily in 15-30 minutes; ML finds good solutions, but proving optimality still needs B&B; instances share size, structure and variable identities (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Replace the single ExtraTrees model of Alvarez et al. with per-variable or per-group models (per generator, time or name), with fallback to the single model when data are scarce (pp. 4-7).
assumptions: Fixed problem structure across instances; 5 MATPOWER-based SCUC networks x 50 randomized variations (40 train / 10 test), up to about 413k variables (pp. 2, 5-6).
proof_devices: n/a (no proofs); evaluation design: textbook Julia B&B without cuts, given the optimal primal value, best-bound with plunging, RB:100:inf oracle, log strong-branching score labels (pp. 4-6)
experiments: 5-fold CV MSE (one network shown); relative MIP gap after 1,000 nodes (ML:PV 0.40% vs ML:ET 0.54% vs RB 0.31%) and after 10,000 nodes (0.29% vs 0.45%); fallback rates; robustness with presolved test instances; no running times (pp. 8-12).
positioning: Modifies Alvarez-Louveaux-Wehenkel ML:ET; GNN advantage judged unclear for fixed structure; GPU strong branching orthogonal; cites own group's B&B theory (pp. 3, 6, 12).
writing: Framed as a 'simple modification'; labelling cost called negligible; skipping timing justified as 'self-evident, in our opinion' (pp. 1-2, 8).
limits_future: Names the accuracy-vs-coverage trade-off; future: other ML branching methods, train small / test large, cuts and primal heuristics, other operational problems such as OTS; SCUC only and no wall-clock evidence (pp. 10, 12-13).

title: Branch-and-bound solves random binary IPs in poly(n)-time
contribution: With best-bound node selection and any variable-branching choice, branch-and-bound solves random packing binary IPs with a fixed number of constraints in polynomially many nodes with good probability; a deterministic corollary bounds the tree for any well-behaved 0/1 IP.
problem_entry: Variable-branching B&B works well in practice despite exponential worst cases; avoid the worst case by analysing random instances, as smoothed analysis did for simplex (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Tree size <= 2|G|n+1, where G is the set of 0/1 points with reduced-cost gap <= IPGap (deterministic); then count G on random data using the small integrality gap and few columns near the Lagrangian hyperplane (Thm 3 p. 7; Thm 1 pp. 2-3).
assumptions: A, c i.i.d. uniform [0,1], m fixed, b = beta*n with beta < 1/2, packing form, best-bound node selection, any fractional variable, only pruning by bound counted (pp. 2-3).
proof_devices: best-bound never branches below IP* (Lemma 1, pp. 4-5)
at most m fractional coordinates at an LP vertex (Lemma 2, p. 5)
node -> good-point charging, injective along root paths via a lowest-common-ancestor argument (Lemmas 4-5, pp. 7-8)
reduced-cost gap bounded below by column distance to the hyperplane, distances bucketed in powers of 2 (Lemmas 6-7, pp. 8-10)
uniform slab bound via epsilon-net + Bernstein + Ball cube slicing + union bound (Thm 4, pp. 11-13)
Dyer-Frieze integrality gap O(log^2 n / n) (Thm 2, p. 5)
positioning: Contrasted with Lenstra / Pataki-Tural-Wong basis reduction (heavy machinery rarely used in practice) and custom enumeration schemes (Lueker, Goldberg-Marchetti-Spaccamela, Beier-Vocking, Dyer-Frieze) that are not standard B&B; cites follow-ups Borst et al. and Frieze (p. 3).
writing: Claims a first result for standard B&B but calls its practical reading an 'indication'; lists reasons practice should do better than the theorem; version paragraph quantifies the improvement over SODA (pp. 1, 3-4).
limits_future: Corollary 3 defines 'well-behaved' IPs (small integrality gap, few columns near a hyperplane); limits: m fixed, uniform packing data, best-bound only, no tightness or lower-bound discussion, no future-work section (pp. 2-3, 15).

title: Sensitivity Analysis for Mixed Binary Quadratic Programming
contribution: Approximating the change in the optimal MBQP value under rhs changes is NP-hard; strong duality for Burer's CPP reformulation and its copositive dual holds when P is bounded or Q is PSD (with a closed-form epsilon-optimal dual, a gap example otherwise and non-attainment in general); choosing a good epsilon-optimal dual via a DNN restriction gives better rhs-sensitivity bounds than Shor-type duals.
problem_entry: Operational MBQPs are re-solved with a changing rhs; solvers find primal solutions fast but not dual bounds; IP sensitivity (Cook et al.) is trivial for binaries (pp. 2, 40).
key_idea: Use copositive dual solutions as rhs-parametric bounds; since the epsilon-optimal dual set is never a singleton and KK_i blocks worsen the bound by (Delta b_i)^2, search the epsilon-optimal face for a dual with small KK_i weight (Thm 3 p. 5; Prop 5 and Remark 3, pp. 9-10; eqs. 9-12, pp. 10-12).
assumptions: Standard form with x >= 0 and assumption (A) (the linear constraints imply 0 <= x_j <= 1 for binaries); strong duality needs P bounded or Q PSD; local stability (Thm 4) is the hinge and fails when Q is not PSD and P is unbounded (pp. 4-8).
proof_devices: two-sided (Gamma1, Gamma2) approximation definition plus reduction from 3-edge-colourability of cubic graphs (pp. 3, 16-18)
strict copositivity of H gives a Slater point (pp. 18-19)
local stability via a finite polyhedral decomposition and Vavasis's QP characterization, giving a piecewise-quadratic value function (pp. 19-23)
penalty building blocks KK_i, G_j acting like augmented-Lagrangian penalties, three-case copositivity split (pp. 23-33)
positive constants from auxiliary LPs and a Charnes-Cooper linear-fractional LP (pp. 25-27)
non-attainment on the 6-clique stable-set dual via test vectors and epsilon sandwiching (pp. 33-36)
experiments: Five generated classes (COMB, KBQP, SSLP, SSQP, PACK); baselines Shor1, Shor2, Cont; relative gap to the exact z(b+Delta b) normalized by Shor1; Julia/Gurobi/Mosek on a PC; the 'tightest in all cases' claim fails at Delta k = 1 for COMB (1.28 vs Shor1 = 1, Cont 0.90) (pp. 12-16, 40-43).
positioning: Builds on Burer's CPP reformulation and Guo-Bodur-Taylor's shadow-price use; part (a) credited to Brown et al.; parts (b)-(d) claimed new; IP sensitivity literature shown inadequate for binaries (pp. 2, 5).
writing: Results with proof sketches first, full proofs later; a notation table for constants; each part of the theorem followed by a 'cannot be improved' remark; computations labelled preliminary; an introduction claim backed by an appendix table (pp. 3, 5, 8, 18, 40).
limits_future: Size limited by the SDP solver; no guarantee for replacing COP by S+ + SP; loose constants; future: generalized copositive reformulations of QCQPs, scalable SDP, cutting planes using the Thm 3(b) structure (pp. 28, 36-37).
